Knowledge/12-Week.title: 12 Week
Knowledge/12-Week.content:
Why
For many years I have operated on yearly plans. Then I would break those down to quarters then weeks then days. The issue with this was that it encouraged me to take a year to make meaningful change.
This also meant that if I slipped up one quarter it was fine because the “deliverable” wasn’t due till year end and I could make up for it in the next quarter. This led to some very busy Q4s and less meaningful change standing the test of time.
In school it was much the same just swap in semesters for quarters.
What
The idea of this was from The 12 week year book. Basically the idea is that I needed to have a “right sized” cadence of delivery. Something large enough to make meaningful change but not too large as to encourage procrastination.
I am not married to it being 12 weeks but something in that general area seems about right. They do loosely sync up with quarters.
52 weeks a year
48 weeks a year for execution
4 weeks for planning / downtime
The order goes something like

Week of planning the next 12 week
12 weeks of execution
Week of review / planning / taking a breather
12 weeks of execution
Week of review / planning / taking a breather
12 weeks of execution
Week of review / planning / taking a breather
12 weeks of execution

Toward end of year / beginning of next year the holiday season will end up breaking it up a bit shortening a 12 week here or there but same general plan.
Once again nothing magic about the number 12. Unless of course we consider the sum of its divisors (1, 2, 3, 4, 6) equals 16, which is greater than 12 making 12 the smallest of the abundant numbers
Outcome
Now I aim to build 12 week plans with the following characteristics.

They need to move me meaningfully and sustainably toward the Future

New habit, lifestyle change, big life moves, new skill acquisition, etc.


They must be tangible, measurable in some way.

I usually prefer to have a leading metric be my guide during the 12 week, and a trailing metric inform me if that change is having the effect I was hoping for during planning. I don’t concern myself with the trailing metric when I’m executing the 12 week.


I limit myself to 2 at a time

part of me wishes I could make this one at a time
My 2 are 1 for professional life and 1 for personal

Simplified example from a few years ago

Professional: Move to a large enterprise company
Personal: Move into the city proper

Knowledge/Capture.title: Capture
Knowledge/Capture.content:
What?
Capture for me is making sure that all ideas and requests go to one place so that I can process them at one time. From there they go to die. Few will survive and live on to the done column.
In Practice
Currently I use Notion as my primary capture tool. I have a button on all screens of my phone and a hotkey on my computer that once hit allows me to write down the thought.
These get processed later in Processing for now they sit in an intake list.
Why?
My brain loves to have ideas and generally loves to over value ideas. There are two primary issues that caused me to adopt this Capture system.

I can tell my brain to let it go

I will stay stuck on an idea loving the idea and playing with it in my head like a distracting toy. This takes me off task and away from what I was intending to remain focused on.
This practice allows me to tell my brain: “It’s there we will think about it later now back to task”. If I don’t do this my brain likes to constantly remind me of the idea while working as to now forget it.


I don’t make good investment decisions in the moment


If I allow my mind to make a call right then and there about whether or not I will or will not proceed with some idea or solving some problem I am more likely to spend my time in wasteful a manner.
I generally over value new ideas and find additional time between idea inception and decision making allows me to increase the rationality of my decisions. Especially around how I spend my time.




I’m sure having capture systems has given me more positive benefits than what is listed above. In my professional life where I need to juggle multiple priorities being organized helps. But the above 2 are my primary reasons why I put up with the toil.

Knowledge/Character-controller---how-to-.title: Character controller - how to make movement feel good
Knowledge/Character-controller---how-to-.content:
Research
Don’t use RigidBody
You don’t want physics you want to simulate the parts of physics that apply. Use KinimaticBodies instread
Buffer jumps
If I miss my ground check due to miliseconds. Timer when jump is pressed in the falling state so that your input doesn’t have to be picture perfect.
Coyote Time
Have the falling state watch for a jump input right after it takes over and if it sees the jump button press in that time let it take over.
Slide player jump on ledge
Put raycasts above the player’s head and if the outer is free but inner and opposite aren’t slide the player toward the free one to avoid them hitting their head.
Custom Jump implementation
Many things are done here, recommendation is to have a look at a 30 min GDC video about jump mechanics.
Fall Fast
Have gravity higher when you are falling on the jump
Partial jumps
How long you press the jump button is how much of your max height jump you’ll get.
Watching the GDC Talk on Jumps
GDC Math for Game Programmers - Building a better jump

Seems to indicate that some understanding of the gaps you need to jump over are important to tune your jump
Mario tripled gravity at the peak of his jump
Having a min jump height when you got to implement something like Fall Fast
Euler integration is the idea of multiplying the acceleration and position by delta time

Downsides is

Unstable - need to read into that
Causes instability




Runge-Kutta - RK4

See Gaffer on Gamer: “Integration Basics”
Very complex implementation


Velocity Verlet

If you hold acceleration constant then you can simplify this function further - error of using this approach even when non constant the error is very small
The simplified formula for the jump was: acc is the acceleration due to gravity

You should have the horizontal component of velocity remain when jump is activated this only affects the vertical velocity change





pos += velocity * delta + 1/2 * accel * delta * delta
vel += acc * delta

Knowledge/Developing-taste-is-the-first-.title: Developing taste is the first step of mastery
Knowledge/Developing-taste-is-the-first-.content:
Intro
Mastery may not be the right word - virtuoso - perhaps a better term. But leaving that aside. To become great you need a couple of things. Where you are, an idea of where to go, and a way to measure whether you got closer or further from the goal. Chief among these is knowing if you got closer or further. You need a compass.
Body


The map of any improvement


The ways to improve

repetitions
quality of reps

coach - where to focus
taste - what is most wrong in the sea of wrong


The plateau



The predicate themselves on knowing what is better than where you are now - that is taste


Large jumps in quality are easily perceptible but you don’t improve by large leaps, you make incremental steps. Incremental steps make smaller changes in quality. Smaller changes in quality are harder to taste. To be able to evaluate your improvement you must be able to taste those small incremental steps. The better your taste the tighter your feedback loop, the tighter the loop the more rapid your improvement.


Large jumps in quality → easy taste


Improvement → small jumps in quality


Small jumps in quality → hard taste


tight Feedback loop → rapid improvement


slow feedback loop → slow improvement


Rapid Improvements (or higher quality) → Tight feedback loop → smaller jumps in quality (incremental) → harder to taste


Thus

Better taste → tighter you can make your feedback loop
Tighter feedback → more rapid improvement and higher quality improvements



Conclusion

Knowledge/Difficulty-Curves-and-video-ga.title: Difficulty Curves and video games
Knowledge/Difficulty-Curves-and-video-ga.content:
Don’t just have a linear increasing curve, exponential curves are good for easy enter high mastery outcomes that lends itself to competitive games.
People become desensitized to stimuli over time so an ever increasing difficulty will no longer get the response your looking for they will get bored or frustrated.
An increasing curve that has levels of falloff after introducing a new mechanic would allow the player to get used to the mechanic before you are testing them super hard.
The following approach to creating a distribution is effectively using cut points on a curve then multiplying by a weight to skew them a bit to make larger or smaller numbers more likely. then they normalize that back into range by dividing it via proportions relative to the other numbers generated.
func weighted_partition(n: int, total: float, weights: Array, power: float) -> Array:
    var raw = []
    var sum_raw = 0.0
    
    for i in range(n):
        var val = pow(randf(), power) * weights[i]
        raw.append(val)
        sum_raw += val
    
    var result = []
    for val in raw:
        result.append(val / sum_raw * total)
    return result
Power raising on a number that is 0 < x < 1 behaves quite differently than x > 1. Having a high power actually pushes it away from one whereas lower powers pull it closer to one.
I will likely have it such that my game actually changes the power and weights used based on some vetted difficulty options. One that gives you a demanding resource one that gives you an even split (most of the time) etc.

The little undo circle in the inspector means you’ve changed a value on that instance from it’s original (scene) value
There is a mention here about resources which are another essentail building block of GoDot but one they will cover later
Due to instancing the team recommends building the following for your game


Scripting

scripts inherit all properties and functions of their parent
Every script is implicitly a class. Using the extends keyword at the top is how you set your parent

RefCounted is the default base class which seems to be the base class handling memory management in the engine


Naming convention is snake case in the scripts and Title case in the inspector - they transform the names there
The docs claim that member variables sit after extends and before the functions but in testing I was able to get vars to “hoist” so I think they have hoisting in the scripting language
_process() is a virtual function in the Node class which is called every frame

delta will be passed to _process to give you the time that has past between cycles


In built functions that communicate with the engine start with an _
There isn’t a this keyword to get to properties you inherit so var names just exist that you need to know are properties of your parents ex rotation in this case
# is the comment character in the scripting lang

Listening for Input

Input is a singleton managed by GoDot to respond / gain access to key presses and other input from the user
Project → Project Settings → Input map is the place with the strings mapped to inputs for various controller input types

ui_left and ui_right are always predefined and map to d pad on controllers and arrow keys on keyboard


There is an _unhandled_input which can be used to make callbacks for key pressing which won’t be pressed every frame - they gave the example of space to jump

Signals

They are first class having the type Signal
_on_node_name_signal_name is the convention for signal handler functions
You can wire them in the node panel (over on the right window it’s a tab next to inspector)

This is only possible for nodes that you make through the editor and won’t work for nodes you instantiate through code, for that you need code wiring of the signals


the Node class has a function set_process which will control whether or not the _process function will be getting called in the game loop
_ready is the internal function that is called once the node is fully instantiated
the Node class get_node function does a lookup of children by name
the visible property will control if the node is visible on screen
if you want a timer to start automatically you need to set Autostart on the timer
You can connect to signals with the connect function on the Signal
Emit a signal by calling emit() on that signal

You can make your own Signal to emit a custom signal
signal health_changed(old_value, new_value)

this is an example definition of a signal on a node
From the docs looks like signal params are the wild west, they don’t’ enforce you can only have matching number of params when you emit





My first 2D Game

You set your project’s veiwport setting in Project Settings → Window → Size

For this game it’s 480 x 720 so a portrait game
Under scale you control the way the game scales to different size screens. We’ve set to preserve aspect ration with the Keep setting. And canvas_items which I need to read what that does.

Canvas items mode will scale the Images then render, veiwport renders then scales





Player Scene

Important note when making a scene, you make your root the type of node that you want your scene to be used as.

In this example a player is a 2DArea since we primarily are using it to detect when something comes into it’s area, along with this we attach animated sprite and a collider to facilitate the above.


That common error I was seeing when making a 2DArea the root node was due to 2 parts. One it needs a collider on it - under shape. but usually you want to hook up your visual prior to collider so that you can make the hitbox match the visual. In this they use an AnimatedSprite2D

Scripting player movement

The $NodeName is the equivalent of making the get_node(NodeName) call
it’s important to remember the viewport is actually in the 4th quadrant of a Cartesian coordinate plane but the Y axis is flipped. so that means that going “down” is actually adding to the y access

Why, why they do this must be a reason to basically mirror the graph upside down up and right is (+,-) and down and left is (-,+) that is going to shake my brain for a bit


you can grab the screen size vector2 by making a call to get_viewport_rect which gives you a Vector2 of the screen
Mapping input as we’ve seen before in in the second tab of project settings, give it a name and map inputs to that you call in code using Input and can just if action is pressed or just pressed etc.

Animating Player

set the current animation by grabbing the AnimationPlayer and setting the animation property on it
You can have movement shown by controlling the flip_h and flip_v properties to show velocity of movement.
when not moving be sure to call stop() on the animation player. (or setting to an idle animation)

Player Collisions

a custom signal can be created using signal keyword, usually defined with properties at top of file

calling emit() on that signal will have the signal emitted to listeners


You can use Node panel on inspector to wire the _on_body_entered callback and provide logic for handling the player collision with another object

Note that when setting physics properties in _process you should use set_deffered otherwise there are race conditions with the physics loop.



Mob Scene
Scene Setup

make the same setup as player but including a notifier that I haven’t used yet - will see later what that is
Looks like scale should be set on the lowest level item that needs to scale ie. the sprites are big so scale the AnimatedSprite2D not the root node.
Animation speed can be changed by adjusting the FPS on the animation player on a per animation basis

Mob Script

Would seem the LSP is still in the needs some work phase

	var animations = Array($AnimatedSprite2D.sprite_frames.get_animation_names())

This line was basically accepting anything after sprite_frames


Array has a useful rand function on it called pick_random which is being used to pick a random animation.
I currently call play in the _ready function because I assume I want this thing animating once it comes in but maybe I’ll handle that elsewhere when we get to spawning them



Main Scene
Scene Setup

Use the node type since we don’t need location data for the main scene
Using the Path2D we can make a path around the scene which in combination with the PathFollow2D will act as our spawn location
Timers can be set to one shot which means they will just run once. Useful for the start of game delay

Main Script

I need to refresh my radian math
Auto completely being mad bugged up is going to bause a many bugs I see it already, the thing doesn’t even know what linear_velocity is. I think there must be a typing systems here that I could then use to make that better since this lang isn’t actually statically styped
doing signal emiting and tying into timers timeouts is easy I’m quite comfortable with it.
Directional math needed to spawn the mobs I understand what we are doing but I am not comfortable enough in radian based math to see the angles in my head, need to refresh there.

HUD

CanvasLayer is the root node for the UI
Control is the base class for UI elements
Buttons and things work exactly how I would expect from working on other UI frameworks
you can await a timer using await syntax like promises

await $MessageTimer.timeout will have you suspend till that timeout occurs
You can pragmatically create timers with get_tree().create_timer(duration)


You can create groups which allow you to signal to a group of instances, in the mob case we add mob scene to the mob group and that allows the following

get_tree().call_group("group_name","function_name") which allows for group signaling


AudioStreamPlayer can be used to add music to the game
Using ColorRec or TextureRec you can add background to the game

Conclusion
I think I’ve got enough of an understanding of the fundamentals that I could get an asset pack / make one for myself and create a similar level difficulty game myself without a guide. I think I’ll hold off on the next section of learning - “First 3D Game”. Since I don’t have plans to use the 3D engine yet. I’d like to make make sure I can make 2D games as simple as this but with my own ideas.

Knowledge/Supercommunicators.title: Supercommunicators
Knowledge/Supercommunicators.content:
Background
This is a nonfiction practical book.
Supercommunicators titled thus to imply there are those who have a near super human ability to communicate. Communication is a super power.

Definition of Supercommunicators - they are able to connect with anyone

people we love talking to
they make us feel heard
we turn to them for advice



This book aims to answer the question of what certain people are doing that when you finish talking to them you feel better, more centered, smarter, etc. (pg xv)

Three types of conversation

practical

What’s this really about?


emotional

How do we feel?


social

Who are we?




Matching

Recognizing and matching each conversation
Listening hear complex emotion



Each of the following sections delves into one of the three aforementioned types of communication

Each section seems to open with some broad idea
then pulls in a case study
Then ends in a “guide to using these ideas”

Question: how to handle emotional conversations

Asserts that the best way to begin an emotional conversation is to ask a deep question

A deep question is one that asks about or has the other person talk about their beliefs, experiences, values, or feelings
Puts forward three characteristics of deep questions

Be about experience, values, and judgement
how they feel
Reveals something


Watch for non linguistic emotional expressions

Pacing
Tone
Gestures
Expression


When listening for the response to a deep question watch for the following

Mood
Energy




Once you have done the above you should loop for understanding

Ask a question
Repeat back what you heard in your own words - distill what you’ve heard
Ask if you got it right
Repeat till yes


Benefits of this are summarized into a statement “Reciprocal Vulnerability” - two benefits to this looping

You’ve shown that you have listened, corrects it if wrong
You’ve shown that you cared enough to do so
How to reciprocate vulnerability

Looping for understanding
Looking for what someone needs
Asking permission
Giving something in return





Summery of my thoughts
Open with a deep question, one that makes them reveal something such that I can learn what it is they want from conversation. I should be listening to the mood and energy of the response to help me dial in how they are feeling and what they want from me.
Based on the above it seems that the author puts forward a premise of being more explicit about what you are hearing from the person will help. For instance, looping for understanding step 3 (after asking question and listening), you are distilling what you’ve heard back to them so that you get their confirmation that they have been heard. Likewise, there is a step of asking for permission in the reciprocate vulnerability idea that seems to also move more toward an explicit nature.
Overall, Better questions, more explicit responses. Listen better such that you can reduce number of cycles needed to get confirmation of understanding.
Preface
Follows the story of a famed FBI negotiator Felix Sigala.
When the scienctists that were trying to understand Felix Sigala asked him how he thinks about communication he told them it’d be easier to show them. He

Recipricated their vulnerabilites by sharing similar times

This is interesting from the perspective of the conflict of always making it about yourself but also needing to balence recipricating vulnerabilites.


He asked questions, lots of em
He showed them he heard them

he then claimed the reason that they were willing to be vulnerable was because fo the environment he created with them. That had led to them being conmfortable enough to share.
neural entrainment first mentioned on pg xv

Knowledge/The-Way-I-Work-v2.title: The Way I Work v2
Knowledge/The-Way-I-Work-v2.content:
Background
The purpose of “the way I work” series of writing is to track what my process actually is.
Personally I use it as a bit of an audit. My workflow goes through expansions and contractions naturally. “The way I work” is a practice I do to help with contracting my workflow and distilling it down to the essential parts.


                  
                  Simplification 
                  
                

If you force me to write down my process it will become much more simple… Because I’m lazy, and I use that to my advantage


So I write this for me with the goal of simplification. Others may find it useful as a way to see how I work and steal parts for themselves.


                  
                  Adopt with Caution 
                  
                

The way we work is very personal. Two recommendations:

Don’t adopt multiple things at once, resist that urge. Add most valuable thing first, evaluate it’s effect, keep or discard, and then repeat.
Take the WHY of my process and ask yourself it applies to you. The specifics of how I do it are irrelevant, the notes I take, capture systems imployed, etc. don’t matter as much as the thing I’m trying to do and how my systems help me do it.



The Core
The way I view my system today is through the lens of two buckets.
Cadence
The goal is to make sure that I balance short term and long term thinking. While also ensuring I don’t spend too much time on “meta” work. I want the vast majority of my time going towards actually doing.
Practices
Things that help me DO. They facilitate an outcome.
My Cadences

 I should make my cadences be the parent instead of everything having The Way I Work v2 as the parent

Future

A current working view of the future, anytime I’m planning or making decisions I keep this view in mind
It’s action based not outcome based - see Future for more details

Yearly

Reflect on the year

Trackers

Really don’t care which one currently using ___ but need to measure to change.

So long as I can record quantity, yes/no style and show me my history I’m satisfied. Everything after that is bonus or fluff.





                  
                  Peter Drucker 
                  
                

If you can’t measure, it you can’t manage it


Alarms

Used for time ques

Caffeine alarm
morning alarm
night shutdown



Working in Public

The newest addition to the way I work

Implementation
Tools in use
Here is an idea of the tools I currently use for each of my practices. At some point I’ll update pages on each of them to explain key features of why I use that particular tool. Note that 99% of the time the tool doesn’t matter. There is a workflow I’m trying to maintain an I pick tools that fit that workflow, if multiple can then I.

Background
link
Anki is composed of two core concepts. Spaced repetition and active recall learning. Active recall has been shown to improve long term retention.

 find the source of the active recall being better than passive  [completion:: 2025-09-06]

Improving Students’ Learning With Effective Learning Techniques
Seems anecdotally true in my experience but ground it
2013 review “Improving Students’ Learning With Effective Learning Techniques” by John Dunlosky and colleagues is one of the most frequently cited papers on this topic

Karpicke and Roediger (2008): In a widely referenced study, college students who used self-testing after learning material retained 80% of it, compared to only 30% for students who only reviewed the content.
Agarwal et al. (2017): A review of studies involving undergraduates found that active recall consistently produced better long-term outcomes than passive reading across disciplines such as psychology and anatomy.
Ebersbach et al. (2020): This study on university students found that those who used retrieval practice scored an average of 11 percentage points higher on a final test compared to students who only restudied the material.
Retrieval practice in real classrooms (August 2025): A study published in Translational Issues in Psychological Science found that retrieval practice implemented in a real primary school setting significantly enhanced learning compared to passive methods, even when young students were involved





Passive recall has a 75% knowledge loss in the first two weeks.

 find source for that claim  [completion:: 2025-09-06]

It’s a potential over simplification of the Hermann Ebbinghaus in the late 19th century paper - forgetting curve - read into that paper.
1885 book,Über das Gedächtnis (“On Memory”). It was later translated into English as Memory -  A Contribution to Experimental Psychology



Spaced repetition is primarily used as the mechanism to lower review effort. As amount of cards grows reviewing all of them is too cumbersome. Finding the optimal path of least frequent review solves for this.

Given the 75% fall off is there something there about time duration in between reviews or is it merely a function of time - spacing effect

 look into the spacing effect and whether only time is needed or if there is something to not reviewing in the space between  [completion:: 2025-09-06]

Memory -  A Contribution to Experimental Psychology






In fact, studies show we forget about 75% of material learned within a 48 hour period


The spacing effect was reported in 1885 by a German psychologist called Hermann Ebbinghaus.


in 1972, when a German scientist called Sebastian Leitner popularized a method of spaced repetition with paper flashcards

SuperMemo was Anki’s precursor but it was not open source, did not give you control of data, and only supported windows along with being rather hard to use / buggy this led to Anki.
There are two algorithms at play in Anki a legacy one and the new one.

 what are the anki algorithm names what was the reason for the change?  [completion:: 2025-09-06]

SM-2 is the default it was taken from SuperMemo
FSRS is claimed to be the more efficient algorithm as it represents

Retrieve-ability (R) - probability of users retention
Stability (S) - time in days for R to decrease from 100% to 90%
Difficulty (D) - difficulty of the content
I’ll turn it on and try it out see how it does. They claim it leads to same level of retention with less reviews.





Getting Started
link

Do not learn if you do not understand.
—SuperMemo

Anatomy of Anki, a card is a question answer pair. A note is an entry of fields and a note type. A note can then create many cards. A deck is a collection of cards. A collection is all of your things in Anki. Card types are templates that tell Anki how to make cards from the fields you have on a note. There are note types as well. Note types control what fields a note has and what card types will be generated on those notes. You can have one note type for a note entry. But then could have many card types on that note type such that one note creates many cards.
Card states are the various statuses a card can be in.
New


Cards that have been added but not yet reviewed
Learning


Cards that have done a review but are not yet known - you did one review recently
Review


Young

Cards who’s interval is < 21



Mature

Cards who’s Interval is > 21
Relearning



Cards who were learned but then forgotten they go back to learning

Knowledge/Writing-combats-ignorance-of-y.title: Writing combats ignorance of your own knowledge
Knowledge/Writing-combats-ignorance-of-y.content:
Overestimation of current knowledge is my greatest threat in my learning.
When I go to learn a skill I find that Developing taste is the first step of mastery, this is very apparent with concrete application based skills. The conundrum I face with theory based knowledge is that I don’t have a clear path on how to evaluate my own knowledge nor improve my taste for that field.
When learning to cook there is a very clear path to beat Dunning Kruger Effect, eat good food. As you do this you develop a taste for what good truly is. Then you can taste food you cook and it is very clear you have a long way to go.
The same is true of music and many other application based skills. However, what do you do for theory skills? How does one improve their “taste” for Philosophy? The only answer I’ve had in the past was reading. Read those who are great. That will develop your taste as you start to understand the viewpoints and ways of thinking of the greats. But once you have that taste - if reading even does truly develop it[^1] - how do you evaluate yourself?
This is why I write: crafting a thesis, making a case, and defending it gives me a concrete artifact to evaluate my understanding. I then observe how hard it was to write and formulate and defend, how much referencing or research did I have to do to write that, etc.
Writing is my answer to the case, How does one prove knowledge of the theoretical to themselves.

Knowledge/spaced-repetition-system.title: Spaced Repetition System
Knowledge/spaced-repetition-system.content:
What am I doing with this?
What I use this for is effectively my takeaways. Things that resonate with me. Ah Ha moments or key insights and learnings that I want to recall the specifics of so that they are committed to memory. It’s been expanding as of late but for now that should suffice an explanation of how I use it.
My current system of choice is Anki - link

Note I have very limited opinions on one tool over the other in this space

What is all of this about?
I am not qualified enough to really explain this one. For me it’s an area I’m currently exploring.
So
Let me point you in the direction that peaked my interest enough for me to adopt this method.


                  
                  Make sources for quantum Country and notes 
                  
                

Andy Matuschak

Andy’s Spaced Repetition Notes
A stack of notes from Andy that form a compelling case to me

There were compelling enough to at least warrant a trial for me in a broader use case than just foreign language vocabulary



Micheal Neilson

Augmenting Long-term Memory - link to the post

The above two authors worked on a project quantum country that I find fascinating. link to quantum country. Find more about it here Andy’s notes on it

Sources/Brandon-Boswell-Year-in-Review.title: Brandon Boswell Year in Review
Sources/Brandon-Boswell-Year-in-Review.content:
His 2022 Year in review
Something about this spoke to me when I saw it. As time goes on you’ll forget much of a year. I like the idea of aggregating at multiple levels. Things that really stick with you in a day go in a day note, things that stuck in a week go in week note, stuck in “chunk” be that quarter, semester, or 12 week go in that note, and then a year note.
I can imagine myself looking back at this when I’m 125 and being thankful I have these. P.S. future Quinn if you’re reading this at 125, confirmed beer is a preservative
